stories.body: US prosecutors have charged three men with coordinating attacks and attempted attacks in support of Iran’s Revolutionary Guard and Iraq’s Kataib Hezbollah, including an alleged September plot against RAF Fairford, which housed US aircraft and personnel. Prosecutors say the preparations included surveillance, vans, fuel barrels and metal objects intended as shrapnel. One defendant allegedly relayed coded instructions from detention in New York through calls to relatives. The indictment also links the men to attacks against Jewish communities in Europe. British police found petrol but no explosives in the vans near Fairford. Iran has denied involvement in the incident.
stories.headline: US charges three alleged Iran-backed operatives over RAF Fairford plot

stories.body: Gadi Eisenkot and allied opposition parties are moving to replace the Knesset speaker and advance legislation establishing a state inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attacks, introducing prime ministerial term limits and reversing parts of Benjamin Netanyahu’s judicial overhaul. Eisenkot has 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension, but divisions among potential partners leave a coalition uncertain. President Isaac Herzog urged concessions to avoid another election. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister and attacked Palestinian-led parties during the opening session. Election authorities have dismissed allegations of irregularities affecting the result.
stories.headline: Israeli opposition moves to secure October 7 inquiry as new parliament opens

stories.body: British counter-terrorism police arrested a 41-year-old senior US Army soldier near Gloucester on Tuesday on suspicion of obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting Russian intelligence. The BBC reports that he was based at Imjin Barracks, headquarters of NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. Officers are searching two locations in Gloucestershire, and the soldier remains in custody in London. Police say the investigation is separate from other ongoing cases. He was detained under the National Security Act, which allows detention without charge for up to 14 days.
stories.headline: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence

stories.body: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele says his forces destroyed a compound used by Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang in a ground and air operation outside Port-au-Prince. Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé welcomed the operation. The BBC could not independently verify Bukele’s video, the building’s identity or the extent of the damage, and reported deaths remain unconfirmed. El Salvador deployed more than 2,000 soldiers after four air force technicians working with a UN-backed mission were abducted in October. The deployment has prompted questions about coordination with that mission and the rules governing Salvadoran operations.
stories.headline: El Salvador says its forces destroyed Haitian gang headquarters

stories.body: The Global Carbon Project forecasts a 0.4% fall in fossil-fuel carbon dioxide emissions this year, driven by renewable-energy growth and reduced oil demand following the Iran war’s energy shock. Oil-related emissions are projected to fall 1.9% and gas emissions 0.3%, while coal emissions rise 0.6%. China’s emissions are expected to decline by almost 1%, with decreases also forecast in the US and EU, while India’s rise 4.4%. Researchers caution that a lasting global peak remains uncertain and that sustained reductions require faster adoption of clean energy, electric vehicles and industrial changes.
stories.headline: Global fossil-fuel emissions forecast to fall 0.4% in 2026

stories.body: The House voted 211–204 to refer impeachment articles against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Republican-led Judiciary Committee, effectively shelving the effort for the remaining congressional term. Thomas Massie, who introduced the eight articles, was the only Republican to oppose referral. His resolution accuses Hegseth of conducting the Iran war without congressional approval and overseeing unlawful killings in strikes on suspected drug-trafficking boats. Hegseth dismissed the effort as sabotage, and President Trump backed him. Democrats could pursue impeachment when they take control of Congress in January.
stories.headline: House Republicans block Hegseth impeachment effort over Iran war

stories.body: Democratic gains in state governments have opened a possible path to activating the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact before the 2028 presidential election. Members would award their electoral votes to the national popular-vote winner once participating states hold at least 270 electoral votes. Current members hold 222. Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin, together with either Arizona or Nevada, would clear the threshold, and all five states will have unified Democratic control next year. Several incoming leaders have expressed interest, but legislative timing remains unsettled and supporters anticipate legal challenges.
stories.headline: Democratic state victories could bring popular-vote compact to its threshold

stories.body: Jim Jordan defeated Steve Scalise 106–73 in a secret ballot to become House Republican leader, according to US media reports. The hardline Trump ally replaces Mike Johnson following Republican losses in both chambers in last week’s midterm elections and will lead House Republicans in the minority.
stories.headline: Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader after midterm losses

stories.body: A Washington Post review of records exposed in a Department of Homeland Security hack identified at least 19 ICE recruits hired despite warning signs in their backgrounds. The investigation found that some immigration officers recruited during last year’s rapid hiring drive had histories involving misconduct or criminality.
stories.headline: Investigation finds at least 19 ICE recruits were hired despite warning signs

stories.body: US inflation slowed in October, helped by falling gasoline prices, according to The Washington Post. Food prices rose at a faster pace, leaving continued pressure on household grocery budgets.
stories.headline: US inflation slows in October as gasoline prices fall

stories.body: Youth and Childhood Minister Sira Rego has asked Spain’s data-protection agency to temporarily suspend TikTok after talks with company representatives failed to produce commitments she considered adequate. The request follows a Maldita.es investigation documenting more than 1,000 items of child sexual abuse material with over 48 million views. Rego demanded immediate removal of the material, preservation of evidence and urgent improvements to moderation and recommendation systems. TikTok says it requested the investigation’s full findings to help locate and remove the content. The regulator will decide whether emergency measures are warranted.
stories.headline: Government asks data regulator to suspend TikTok in Spain

stories.body: A National Police canine-unit officer was killed and a bomb-disposal specialist seriously injured when an explosive device in a backpack detonated in Oviedo’s Villafría neighbourhood on Tuesday. Police had responded to a shooting that injured a 17-year-old girl. The injured officer underwent surgery and was reported stable, although his condition remained serious. Investigators suspect the backpack may have been detonated remotely. The search continued into Wednesday for a 64-year-old man known as El Ruso, whom police suspect of carrying out the shooting and placing the device.
stories.headline: Oviedo bomb kills police officer as search for armed suspect continues

stories.body: Authorities ordered the evacuation of Piedralaves, a town of roughly 2,200 people in southern Ávila, on Tuesday because heavy rain threatened to overwhelm the El Horcajo dam. Residents were directed to designated shelters, and 66 care-home residents were moved to other facilities. Extremadura suspended all teaching activity for Wednesday as red rain warnings continued in northern Cáceres and forecasts indicated regional wind gusts of 100–120 km/h. Schools in 32 Ávila municipalities were also closed on Tuesday. Authorities urged residents to limit travel and avoid floodwater and river channels.
stories.headline: Heavy rain prompts Ávila evacuation and school closures across Extremadura

stories.body: The government approved measures expected to provide €820 million a year in additional support to around 760,000 single-parent, low-income large and disabled-parent families. A new national single-parent certificate will establish eligibility for support involving employment, public housing, childcare and social protection. Single parents with two or more children will receive benefits equivalent to those available to large families. The package also extends the highest large-family protection category to households with four children and broadens access to the fund covering unpaid court-ordered child maintenance.
stories.headline: Spain approves €820 million annual support package for vulnerable families

stories.body: Barcelona faces a general strike on Wednesday over housing rights, evictions, pay and working conditions, with demonstrations disrupting roads including the Ronda Litoral. CCOO and UGT are backing the stoppage, which grew out of housing protests following the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid. Pickets began at Mercabarna on Tuesday evening. An afternoon joint demonstration is due to leave Jardinets de Gràcia, with an alternative march starting at Plaça de Jacint Verdaguer. Public transport is affected, and the published metro minimum service is 25% during designated morning and afternoon periods.
stories.headline: General strike brings demonstrations and transport disruption to Barcelona

stories.body: The SEMAF train drivers’ union has postponed the Renfe strike scheduled for Thursday, November 12, until November 23 after the government approved a railway-safety decree. The measures include protection from workplace reprisals for drivers who halt or refuse a journey because of a serious safety risk, alongside stronger safety inspections. The union described the decree as tangible progress and allowed more time for negotiations over outstanding commitments. A separate sector-wide strike on November 17 remains scheduled.
stories.headline: Train drivers move Thursday’s strike to November 23

stories.body: The Barcelona Metropolitan Area approved a €1.358 billion budget for 2027, prioritising public transport, affordable housing and social support. Major allocations include €214.7 million for the metropolitan transport authority, €224.8 million for contracted bus services and €41.2 million for accessible transport and social fares. The metropolitan housing developer IMPSOL has an €88.8 million budget, while €34.2 million is earmarked for school-meal grants and travel assistance. Including public companies such as TMB, the consolidated budget reaches approximately €2.988 billion.
stories.headline: Barcelona metropolitan authority approves €1.358 billion budget for 2027

stories.body: Heavy machinery has begun demolishing the old Palau de Congressos as redevelopment of Fira de Montjuïc advances toward its 2029 centenary. Pavilion 4 has already been demolished, and its site is being prepared for a 20,500-square-metre multifunctional venue using recycled concrete from the demolition. A new congress centre will occupy the renovated Palau d’Alfons XIII, preserving its original structure and adding an auditorium and a garden of around 7,000 square metres. Work at the Palau del Vestit will retain its Plaça d’Espanya colonnade while creating innovation space and a neighbourhood facility.
stories.headline: Demolition advances Montjuïc fairground redevelopment for 2029
